title.zh: 卷三十七 志第七: 地理志一
title.raw: 卷三十七 志第七: 地理志一 Volume 37 Treatises 7: Geography 1

translations.literal: Geography Treatise, Part 1
translations.idiomatic: Geography Treatise I

translations.literal: Emperor Yao divided the realm into Nine Provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Yao divided the world into the Nine Provinces.

sentences.zh: 舜以冀、青地大，分幽、并、營，為州十有二。

translations.literal: Shun, because Ji and Qing were large, split off You, Bing, and Ying, making twelve provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Shun carved You, Bing, and Ying from the oversized Ji and Qing domains, yielding twelve provinces.

sentences.zh: 幽州在渤、碣之間，并州北有代、朔，營州東暨遼海。

translations.literal: You lay between Bo and Jie; north of Bing were Dai and Shuo; Ying reached east to the Liao Sea.
translations.idiomatic: You province lay between the Bo and Jie seas; Bing had Dai and Shuo to its north; Ying extended east to the Liao Sea.

sentences.zh: 其地負山帶海，其民執干戈，奮武衛，風氣剛勁，自古為用武之地。

translations.literal: Its land backed mountains and girded sea; its people took up weapons, roused martial guard; wind and temper were firm and strong—from antiquity a land where armies were deployed.
translations.idiomatic: The region backed mountains and faced the sea; its people took up arms and stood on martial guard; the local temper was hard and bold—a classic military frontier since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 太祖以叠剌部之眾代遙輦氏，起臨潢，建皇都；

translations.literal: Taizu, with the masses of the Dieci tribe, replaced the Yaolian clan, rose at Linhuang, and built the imperial capital;
translations.idiomatic: Taizu, leading the Dieci tribe, supplanted the Yaolian house, raised his seat at Linhuang, and founded the imperial capital;

sentences.zh: 東並渤海，得城邑之居百有三。

translations.literal: east he annexed Bohai and gained one hundred three walled settlements.
translations.idiomatic: to the east he absorbed Bohai and seized one hundred and three walled towns.

sentences.zh: 太宗立晉，有幽、涿、檀、薊、順、營、平、蔚、朔、雲、應、新、媯、儒、武、寰十六州，於是割古幽、并、營之境而跨有之。

translations.literal: Taizong established Jin and held the sixteen prefectures You, Zhuo, Tan, Ji, Shun, Ying, Ping, Yu, Shuo, Yun, Ying, Xin, Gui, Ru, Wu, and Huan—thus cutting the old You, Bing, and Ying tracts and straddling them.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong secured Jin he took sixteen prefectures—You, Zhuo, Tan, Ji, Shun, Ying, Ping, Yu, Shuo, Yun, Ying, Xin, Gui, Ru, Wu, and Huan—so the state spanned the ancient You, Bing, and Ying heartland.

sentences.zh: 東朝高麗，西臣夏國，南子石晉而兄弟趙宋，吳越、南唐航海輸貢。

translations.literal: East he faced Goryeo; west he made the Xia state a vassal; south he treated Later Jin as a son and Song as a brother; Wuyue and Southern Tang sent tribute by sea.
translations.idiomatic: To the east lay Goryeo; to the west the Xia acknowledged subjection; to the south Later Jin was treated as a son-state and Song as a brother; Wuyue and Southern Tang paid tribute by sea.

translations.literal: Alas, how grand it was!
translations.idiomatic: How vast its sway had become!

sentences.zh: 遼國其先曰契丹，本鮮卑之地，居遼澤中，去榆關一千一百三十里，去幽州又七百一十四里。

translations.literal: The Liao state was formerly called Khitan, originally Xianbei land, dwelling in the Liao marshes—1,130 li from Yugu Pass and another 714 li from Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liao's forebears were the Khitan, a Xianbei people living in the Liao marshes—1,130 li from Yugu Pass and 714 li farther from Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 南控黃龍，北帶潢水，冷陘屏右，遼河塹左。

translations.literal: South it controlled Huanglong; north it belted the Huang River; Lengling screened the right; the Liao River trench lay to the left.
translations.idiomatic: To the south it held Huanglong; to the north ran the Huang River; Cold Ridge guarded the west; the Liao River ditch lay on the east.

sentences.zh: 高原多榆柳，下濕饒蒲葦。

translations.literal: The highlands had many elms and willows; the low wetlands abounded in reeds and rushes.
translations.idiomatic: Uplands bore elm and willow; marshy flats were rich in reed and rush.

translations.literal: In Northern Wei times its territory ran several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Northern Wei its domain covered several hundred li.

sentences.zh: 至唐，大賀氏蠶食扶餘、室韋、奚、靺鞨之區，地方二千餘里。

translations.literal: By Tang the Dahe clan nibbled away the lands of Fuyu, Shiwei, Xi, and Mohe until the region reached more than two thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: By Tang the Dahe clan had eaten into Fuyu, Shiwei, Xi, and Mohe territory until their lands exceeded two thousand li.

sentences.zh: 貞觀三年，以其地置玄州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenguan their land was made Xuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan year 3 the court created Xuan Prefecture on their soil.

sentences.zh: 尋置松漠都督府，建八部為州，各置刺史：達稽部曰峭落州，紇便部曰彈汗州，獨活部曰無逢州，芬阿部曰羽陵州，突便部曰日連州，芮奚部曰徒河州，墜斤部曰萬丹州，伏部曰匹黎、赤山二州。

translations.literal: Soon Songmo Protectorate was set up, the eight divisions made into prefectures, each with a cishi: the Daji division as Qiaoluo Prefecture, the Hebian as Danhan, the Duhuo as Wufeng, the Fena as Yuling, the Tubian as Rilian, the Ruixi as Tuhe, the Zhuijin as Wandan, the Fu as Pili and Chishan two prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Songmo Protectorate followed, with eight tribal divisions converted to prefectures, each with a prefect: Daji became Qiaoluo; Hebian became Danhan; Duhuo, Wufeng; Fena, Yuling; Tubian, Rilian; Ruixi, Tuhe; Zhuijin, Wandan; Fu, the twin prefectures Pili and Chishan.

sentences.zh: 以大賀氏窟哥為使持節十州軍事。

translations.literal: The Dahe Kuge was made commissioner with credentials over the ten prefectures' military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Dahe Kuge received credentials as commissioner for military affairs across the ten prefectures.

translations.literal: Dividing prefectures and establishing officials began in this fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Prefecture divisions and official posts took their start here.

sentences.zh: 迨於五代，辟地東西三千里。

translations.literal: By the Five Dynasties they opened land three thousand li east and west.
translations.idiomatic: By the Five Dynasties their domain stretched three thousand li from east to west.

sentences.zh: 遙輦氏更八部曰鳷利皆部、乙室活部、實活部、納尾部、頻沒部、內會雞部、集解部、奚嗢部，屬縣四十有一。

translations.literal: The Yaolian clan renamed the eight divisions Zhilejie, Yishihuo, Shihuo, Nawei, Pinmei, Neihuiji, Jijie, and Xiwu divisions, with forty-one subordinate counties.
translations.idiomatic: The Yaolian house retitled the eight divisions Zhilejie, Yishihuo, Shihuo, Nawei, Pinmei, Neihuiji, Jijie, and Xiwu, governing forty-one counties beneath them.

translations.literal: Each division had a cishi; counties had magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Each division received a prefect; each county a magistrate.

sentences.zh: 太宗以皇都為上京，升幽州為南京，改南京為東京，聖宗城中京，興宗升雲州為西京，於是五京備焉。

translations.literal: Taizong made the imperial capital Shangjing, raised Youzhou to Nanjing, renamed Nanjing to Dongjing, Shengzong walled Zhongjing, Xingzong raised Yunzhou to Xijing—thus the Five Capitals were complete.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong made the imperial seat Shangjing, elevated Youzhou to Nanjing, later renamed it Dongjing; Shengzong built Zhongjing; Xingzong raised Yunzhou to Xijing—completing the Five Capitals.

sentences.zh: 又以征伐俘戶建州襟要之地，多因舊居名之；

translations.literal: They also built prefectures at strategic points with captives from campaigns, often keeping old settlement names;
translations.idiomatic: Campaign captives also seeded prefectures at strategic nodes, often under their former place names;

translations.literal: private slaves were added to establish subordinate-domain prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: private slaves were settled to form subordinate-domain prefectures.

sentences.zh: 總京五，府六，州、軍、城百五十有六，縣二百有九，部族五十有二，屬國六十。

translations.literal: In all: five capitals, six prefectures, one hundred fifty-six prefectures, armies, and walled towns, two hundred nine counties, fifty-two tribal divisions, and sixty subject states.
translations.idiomatic: In total there were five capitals, six superior prefectures, 156 prefectures, armies, and fortified towns, 209 counties, 52 tribal divisions, and 60 subject states.

sentences.zh: 東至於海，西至金山，暨於流沙，北至臚朐河，南至白溝，幅員萬里。

translations.literal: East to the sea, west to the Golden Mountains and on to the shifting sands, north to the Luchiju River, south to the White Ditch—ten thousand li in extent.
translations.idiomatic: Its bounds ran east to the sea, west to the Golden Mountains and the shifting sands, north to the Luchiju River, and south to the White Ditch—a domain of ten thousand li.

translations.literal: ○ Upper Capital Circuit
translations.idiomatic: ○ Shangjing Circuit

sentences.zh: 上京臨潢府，本漢遼東郡西安平之地。

translations.literal: Shangjing Linhuang Prefecture was originally Han Liaodong commandery's Xi'anping land.
translations.idiomatic: Shangjing's Linhuang Prefecture occupied the old Han Liaodong commandery seat of Xi'anping.

translations.literal: Xin Mang called it Beianping.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Mang renamed the place Beianping.

sentences.zh: 太祖取天梯、蒙國、別魯等三山之勢於葦甸，射金齪箭以識之，謂之龍眉宮。

translations.literal: Taizu took the momentum of Tianti, Mengguo, and Bielu three mountains in the reed marsh, shot a gold-tipped arrow to mark it, and called it Longmei Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu seized the heights of Tianti, Mengguo, and Bielu among the reed marshes, marked the site with a gold-notched arrow, and named it Longmei Palace.

sentences.zh: 神冊三年城之，名曰皇都。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shence a city was built, named Huangdu.
translations.idiomatic: In Shence year 3 he walled a city there and called it Huangdu.

sentences.zh: 天顯十三年，更名上京，府曰臨潢。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianxian it was renamed Shangjing; the prefecture was called Linhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxian year 13 the seat became Shangjing and the prefecture Linhuang.

sentences.zh: 淶流河自西北南流，繞京三面，東入於曲江，其北東流為按出河。

translations.literal: The Lailiu River flowed from the northwest southward, encircled the capital on three sides, and entered the Qu River to the east; to the north and east it became the Anchu River.
translations.idiomatic: The Lailiu River ran from the northwest, wrapped the capital on three sides, and entered the Qu River eastward; north and east of the city it formed the Anchu River.

sentences.zh: 又有御河、沙河、黑河、潢河、鴨子河、他魯河、狼河、蒼耳河、輞子河，臚朐河、陰涼河、豬河、鴛鴦湖、興國惠民湖、廣濟湖、鹽濼、百狗濼、火神澱、馬盂山、兔兒山、野鵲山、鹽山、鑿山、松山、平地松林、大斧山、列山、屈劣山、勒得山，唐所封大賀氏勒得王有墓存焉。

translations.literal: There were also the Imperial River, Sha River, Hei River, Huang River, Yazi River, Talu River, Lang River, Canger River, Wangzi River, Luchiju River, Yinyang River, Zhu River, Yuanyang Lake, Xingguo Huimin Lake, Guangji Lake, salt marshes, Baigou Marsh, Huoshen Shoal, Mayu Mountain, Tu'er Mountain, Yaque Mountain, Salt Mountain, Zao Mountain, Song Mountain, Pingdi Pine Forest, Dafu Mountain, Lie Mountain, Qulie Mountain, Lede Mountain—where Tang had enfeoffed the Dahe Lede King and a tomb still stood.
translations.idiomatic: Waters and landmarks included the Imperial, Sha, Hei, Huang, Yazi, Talu, Lang, Canger, and Wangzi rivers; the Luchiju and Yinyang rivers; Zhu River; Yuanyang, Xingguo Huimin, and Guangji lakes; salt marshes; Baigou Marsh; Huoshen Shoal; Mayu, Tu'er, Yaque, Salt, Zao, and Song mountains; the Pingdi pine belt; Dafu, Lie, Qulie, and Lede peaks—the last holding the tomb of the Dahe Lede King enfeoffed by Tang.

sentences.zh: 戶三萬六千五百，轄軍、府、州、城二十五，統縣十。

translations.literal: Households 36,500; it governed twenty-five armies, prefectures, and walled towns and ruled ten counties.
translations.idiomatic: It registered 36,500 households, governed twenty-five armies, prefectures, and fortified towns, and administered ten counties.

translations.literal: Linhuang County.
translations.idiomatic: County seat: Linhuang.

sentences.zh: 太祖天贊初南攻燕、薊，以所俘人戶散居潢水之北，縣臨潢水，故以名。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianzan Taizu attacked south into Yan and Ji and scattered captured households along the north bank of the Huang River; the county faced the Huang River and took its name.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianzan Taizu raided Yan and Ji and settled captives along the Huang River's north bank; the county sat on that river and was named for it.

translations.literal: The soil suited planting.
translations.idiomatic: The land was good for crops.

translations.literal: Households 3,500.
translations.idiomatic: 3,500 households.

translations.literal: Changtai County.
translations.idiomatic: County seat: Changtai.

sentences.zh: 本渤海國長平縣民，太祖伐大諲譔，先得是邑，遷其人於京西北，與漢民雜居。

translations.literal: Originally people of Bohai's Changping County; Taizu, attacking Da Yinzhen, first took this settlement and moved its people northwest of the capital to live mixed with Han.
translations.idiomatic: Its settlers came from Bohai's Changping County; when Taizu attacked Da Yinzhen he seized this town first and resettled its people northwest of the capital among Han households.

translations.literal: Households 4,000.
translations.idiomatic: 4,000 households.

translations.literal: Dingba County.
translations.idiomatic: Dingba County.

sentences.zh: 本扶餘府強師縣民，太祖下扶餘，遷其人於京西，與漢人雜處，分地耕種。

translations.literal: Originally people of Fuyu prefecture's Qiangshi County; Taizu took Fuyu and moved them west of the capital to live mixed with Han, allotting land to farm.
translations.idiomatic: They were originally from Fuyu prefecture's Qiangshi County; after Taizu conquered Fuyu he resettled them west of the capital among Han farmers on divided fields.

sentences.zh: 統和八年，以諸宮提轄司人戶置。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tonghe, households of the various palace supervisory offices were used to establish it.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghe year 8 brought settlers drawn from palace supervisory offices to found the county.

translations.literal: It was subordinate to Changning Palace.
translations.idiomatic: It fell under Changning Palace.

translations.literal: Households 2,000.
translations.idiomatic: 2,000 households.

translations.literal: Baohe County.
translations.idiomatic: Baohe County.

sentences.zh: 本渤海國富利縣民，太祖破龍州，盡徒富利縣人散居京南。

translations.literal: Originally people of Bohai's Fuli County; Taizu took Longzhou and moved all Fuli people scattered south of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Its people came from Bohai's Fuli County; when Taizu seized Longzhou he dispersed Fuli households south of the capital.

sentences.zh: 統和八年，以諸宮提轄司人戶置。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tonghe, households of the various palace supervisory offices were used to establish it.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghe year 8 used households from palace supervisory offices to establish the county.

translations.literal: It was subordinate to Zhangmin Palace.
translations.idiomatic: It belonged to Zhangmin Palace.

translations.literal: Households 4,000.
translations.idiomatic: 4,000 households.

translations.literal: Lu County.
translations.idiomatic: Lu County.

sentences.zh: 本幽州潞縣民，天贊元年，太祖破薊州，掠潞縣民，布於京東，與渤海人雜處。

translations.literal: Originally people of Youzhou's Lu County; in the first year of Tianzan Taizu took Ji Prefecture and carried off Lu County people, placing them east of the capital mixed with Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: They were originally from Youzhou's Lu County; in Tianzan year 1 Taizu captured Ji Prefecture, seized Lu households, and settled them east of the capital among Bohai people.

translations.literal: It was subordinate to Chongde Palace.
translations.idiomatic: It was attached to Chongde Palace.

translations.literal: Households 3,000.
translations.idiomatic: 3,000 households.

translations.literal: Yisu County.
translations.idiomatic: Yisu County.

sentences.zh: 本遼東渤海之民，太平九年，大延琳結構遼東夷叛，圍守經年，乃降，盡遷於京北，置縣居之。

translations.literal: Originally people of Liaodong and Bohai; in the ninth year of Taiping, Da Yanlin stirred the Liaodong Yi to rebel, besieged for a year, then surrendered; all were moved north of the capital and a county was set to house them.
translations.idiomatic: Its founders were Liaodong and Bohai people; in Taiping year 9 Da Yanlin roused Liaodong tribes to revolt, held out a year, then submitted; the court moved them north of the capital and founded a county for them.

sentences.zh: 是年，又徙渤海叛人家屬置焉。

translations.literal: That year families of Bohai rebels were also moved and placed there.
translations.idiomatic: The same year households of Bohai rebels were relocated there as well.

translations.literal: Households 1,000.
translations.idiomatic: 1,000 households.

translations.literal: Qianliao County.
translations.idiomatic: County seat: Qianliao.

sentences.zh: 本遼東諸縣渤海人，大延琳叛，擇其謀勇者置之左右。

translations.literal: Originally Bohai people of Liaodong counties; when Da Yanlin rebelled, the boldest plotters were chosen and placed at the ruler's side.
translations.idiomatic: Originally Bohai from Liaodong counties; during Da Yanlin's revolt the boldest conspirators were kept at court.

sentences.zh: 後以城降，戮之，徙其家屬於京東北，故名。

translations.literal: Later when the city surrendered they were executed; their families were moved northeast of the capital, hence the name.
translations.idiomatic: When the city later surrendered they were executed and their families resettled northeast of the capital—hence the name.

translations.literal: Households 1,000.
translations.idiomatic: 1,000 households.

translations.literal: Bohai County.
translations.idiomatic: Bohai County.

translations.literal: Originally people of Dongjing; because of rebellion they were moved and settled.
translations.idiomatic: Originally Dongjing people, relocated here after a rebellion.

translations.literal: Xingren County.
translations.idiomatic: Xingren County.

translations.literal: Established in the second year of Kaitai.
translations.idiomatic: Founded in Kaitai year 2.

translations.literal: Xuanhua County.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanhua County.

sentences.zh: 本遼東神化縣民，太祖破鴨淥府，盡徙其民居京之南。

translations.literal: Originally people of Liaodong's Shenhua County; Taizu took Yalu Prefecture and moved all its people south of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: They came from Liaodong's Shenhua County; when Taizu seized Yalu Prefecture he moved the entire population south of the capital.

sentences.zh: 統和八年，以諸宮提轄司人戶置。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tonghe, households of the various palace supervisory offices were used to establish it.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghe year 8 settled households from palace supervisory offices to establish the county.

translations.literal: It was subordinate to Zhangmin Palace.
translations.idiomatic: It belonged to Zhangmin Palace.

translations.literal: Households 4,000.
translations.idiomatic: 4,000 households.

translations.literal: Shangjing was the place of Taizu's founding enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Shangjing was Taizu's founding seat.

sentences.zh: 負山抱海，天險足以為固。

translations.literal: Backed by mountains and embracing the sea, heaven's barriers could secure it.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains guarded it and the sea lay before it—natural defenses enough to hold firm.

sentences.zh: 地沃宜耕植，水草便畜牧。

translations.literal: The land was fertile for planting; grass and water favored herding.
translations.idiomatic: Soil was rich for farming; pasture and water favored livestock.

sentences.zh: 金齪一箭，二百年之基，壯矣。

translations.literal: One gold-notched arrow—a foundation of two hundred years—how stout!
translations.idiomatic: A single gold-notched arrow laid a foundation two centuries long—how solid it stood.

sentences.zh: 天顯元年，平渤海歸，乃展郛郭，建宮室，名以天贊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianxian, after pacifying Bohai and returning, the outer walls were extended, palaces built, and the name taken from Tianzan.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxian year 1, after Bohai was pacified, the outer ramparts were expanded, palaces erected, and the complex named for Tianzan.

sentences.zh: 起三大殿：曰開皇、安德、五鸞。

translations.literal: Three great halls were raised: called Kaihuang, Ande, and Wuluan.
translations.idiomatic: Three great halls went up: Kaihuang, Ande, and Wuluan.

sentences.zh: 中有歷代帝王御容，每月朔望、節辰、忌日，在東京文武百官並赴致祭。

translations.literal: Within were portraits of emperors through the ages; on each new and full moon, festival day, and memorial day, civil and military officials of Dongjing all came to offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Inside hung portraits of emperors through the ages; on new and full moons, festivals, and memorial days civil and military officials from Dongjing all came to sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 又於內城東南隅建天雄寺，奉安烈考宣簡皇帝遺像。

translations.literal: In the inner city's southeast corner Tianxiong Temple was built to enshrine the portrait of the late father, Emperor Xuanjian.
translations.idiomatic: At the inner city's southeast corner Tianxiong Temple housed the image of the late Emperor Xuanjian.

sentences.zh: 是歲太祖崩，應天皇后於義節寺斷腕，置太祖陵。

translations.literal: That year Taizu died; Empress Yingtian at Yijie Temple severed her wrist and placed Taizu's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: That year Taizu died; at Yijie Temple Empress Yingtian cut off her wrist and established Taizu's tomb.

translations.literal: The Severed-Wrist Tower was built at the temple and a stele erected.
translations.idiomatic: A Severed-Wrist Tower was raised at the temple with a commemorative stele.

sentences.zh: 太宗援立晉，遣宰相馮道、劉煦等持節，具鹵簿、法服至此，冊上太宗及應天皇后尊號。

translations.literal: Taizong, supporting Jin, sent Chancellor Feng Dao, Liu Xu, and others with credentials, full guard of honor, and court robes here to invest Taizong and Empress Yingtian with honorific titles.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong backed Jin he sent Feng Dao, Liu Xu, and others bearing credentials, full honors, and court robes to invest Taizong and Empress Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 太宗詔蕃部並依漢制，禦開皇殿，辟承天門受禮，因改皇都為上京。

translations.literal: Taizong ordered the tribal ministries to follow Han ritual; he entered Kaihuang Hall, opened Chengtian Gate to receive rites, and therefore changed Huangdu to Shangjing.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong commanded tribal ministries to follow Han ceremony, entered Kaihuang Hall, opened Chengtian Gate for the investiture, and renamed Huangdu Shangjing.

sentences.zh: 城高二丈，不設敵樓，幅員二十七里。

translations.literal: The wall was two zhang high, without watch-towers; the circuit measured twenty-seven li.
translations.idiomatic: Walls stood two zhang high without watch-towers; the circuit ran twenty-seven li.

translations.literal: Gates: east called Yingchun and Yan'er;
translations.idiomatic: Eastern gates: Yingchun and Yan'er;

translations.literal: south called Shunyang;
translations.idiomatic: south: Shunyang;

translations.literal: called Nanfu;
translations.idiomatic: and Nanfu;

translations.literal: west called Jinfeng and Xiyan'er.
translations.idiomatic: west: Jinfeng and Xiyan'er.

sentences.zh: 其北謂之皇城，高三丈，有樓櫓。

translations.literal: The north was called the Imperial City, three zhang high, with towers and parapets.
translations.idiomatic: The northern quarter was the Imperial City—three zhang high with towers and parapets.

sentences.zh: 門，東曰安東，南曰大順，西曰乾德，北曰拱辰。

translations.literal: Gates: east Andong, south Dashun, west Qiande, north Gongchen.
translations.idiomatic: Its gates were Andong east, Dashun south, Qiande west, and Gongchen north.

translations.literal: Within was the Great Inner.
translations.idiomatic: Inside stood the Great Inner.

translations.literal: The inner south gate was Chengtian, with tower-pavilions;
translations.idiomatic: The inner south gate Chengtian had tower-pavilions;

translations.literal: east gate Donghua, west Xihua.
translations.idiomatic: east gate Donghua, west gate Xihua.

translations.literal: These were the passages in and out of the inner precinct.
translations.idiomatic: These were the inner precinct's main passages.

sentences.zh: 正南街東，留守司衙，次鹽鐵門，次南門，龍寺街。

translations.literal: East along the central south avenue: the garrison commissioner's office, next the Salt and Iron Gate, next the south gate, Longsi Street.
translations.idiomatic: Along the main south avenue eastward stood the garrison commissioner's office, then the Salt and Iron Gate, then the south gate and Longsi Street.

sentences.zh: 南曰臨潢府，其側臨潢縣。

translations.literal: South was Linhuang Prefecture; beside it Linhuang County.
translations.idiomatic: To the south lay Linhuang Prefecture with Linhuang County beside it.

sentences.zh: 縣西南崇孝寺，承天皇后建。

translations.literal: Southwest of the county was Chongxiao Temple, built by Empress Chengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Southwest of the county stood Chongxiao Temple, founded by Empress Chengtian.

sentences.zh: 寺西長泰縣，又西天長觀。

translations.literal: West of the temple was Changtai County, and farther west Tianchang Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: West of the temple lay Changtai County and, beyond it, Tianchang Abbey.

sentences.zh: 西南國子監，監北孔子廟，廟東節義寺。

translations.literal: Southwest was the Directorate of Education; north of it Confucius Temple; east of the temple Jieyi Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Southwest stood the Directorate of Education; north of it the Confucius Temple; east of that Jieyi Temple.

sentences.zh: 又西北安國寺，太宗所建。

translations.literal: Farther northwest Anguo Temple, built by Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Farther northwest was Anguo Temple, Taizong's foundation.

sentences.zh: 寺東齊天皇后故宅，宅東有元妃宅，即法天皇后所建也。

translations.literal: East of the temple was the former residence of Empress Qitian; east of that the Yuan Consort residence built by Empress Fatian.
translations.idiomatic: East of the temple stood Empress Qitian's former residence; beyond it the Yuan Consort residence that Empress Fatian built.

sentences.zh: 其南具聖尼寺，綾錦院、內省司、麹院，贍國、省司二倉，皆在大內西南，八作司與天雄寺對。

translations.literal: South were Jushengni Temple, the Brocade Office, Inner Secretariat, Qu Office, and the two granaries Zanguo and Shengsi—all southwest of the Great Inner; the Eight Crafts Office faced Tianxiong Temple.
translations.idiomatic: To the south lay Jushengni Temple, the Brocade Office, Inner Secretariat, Qu Office, and the Zanguo and Shengsi granaries—all southwest of the Great Inner, with the Eight Crafts Office opposite Tianxiong Temple.

sentences.zh: 南城謂之漢城，南當橫街，各有樓對峙，下列井肆。

translations.literal: The south city was called the Han City; facing the cross street south, each had a tower standing opposite, with market stalls below.
translations.idiomatic: The southern quarter was the Han City; along the cross street paired gate-towers faced each other above rows of market stalls.

sentences.zh: 東門之北潞縣，又東南興仁縣。

translations.literal: North of the east gate was Lu County; southeast of that Xingren County.
translations.idiomatic: North of the east gate stood Lu County; southeast of it Xingren County.

sentences.zh: 南門之東回鶻營，回鶻商販留居上京，置營居之。

translations.literal: East of the south gate was the Uighur Camp where Uighur merchants staying at Shangjing were quartered.
translations.idiomatic: East of the south gate lay the Uighur Camp, housing merchants from Uighur lands who traded at Shangjing.

sentences.zh: 西南同文驛，諸國信使居之。

translations.literal: Southwest Tongwen Hostel housed envoys from various states.
translations.idiomatic: Southwest, Tongwen Hostel lodged envoys from foreign states.

sentences.zh: 驛西南臨潢驛，以待夏國使。

translations.literal: Southwest of the hostel was Linhuang Hostel, awaiting Xia envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Southwest of that stood Linhuang Hostel for Xia envoys.

translations.literal: West of the hostel Fuxian Temple.
translations.idiomatic: West of the hostel was Fuxian Temple.

sentences.zh: 寺西宣化縣，西南定霸縣，縣西保和縣。

translations.literal: West of the temple Xuanhua County; southwest Dingba County; west of the county Baohe County.
translations.idiomatic: West of the temple lay Xuanhua County; southwest Dingba; west of that Baohe County.

sentences.zh: 西門之北易俗縣，縣東遷遼縣。

translations.literal: North of the west gate Yisu County; east of the county Qianliao County.
translations.idiomatic: North of the west gate was Yisu County; east of it Qianliao County.

sentences.zh: 周廣順中，胡嶠《記》曰：上京西樓，有邑屋市肆，交易無錢而用布。

translations.literal: In the Guangshun era of Later Zhou, Hu Qiao's Record says: at Shangjing's west tower were houses and market stalls; trade used cloth, not coin.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Qiao's Record from Later Zhou's Guangshun era notes that Shangjing's west tower quarter had houses and markets where cloth served as currency.

sentences.zh: 有綾錦諸工作、宦者、翰林、伎術、教坊、角觝、儒、僧尼、道士。

translations.literal: There were brocade workshops, eunuchs, Hanlin, artisans, music offices, wrestlers, Confucians, monks and nuns, and Daoists.
translations.idiomatic: The city held brocade workshops, eunuchs, Hanlin academicians, artisans, music bureaus, wrestlers, Confucians, monks, nuns, and Daoists.

translations.literal: Chinese were mostly from Bing, Fen, You, and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Han residents came chiefly from Bing, Fen, You, and Ji.

sentences.zh: 宋大中祥符九年，薛映《記》曰：上京者，中京正北八十里至松山館，七十里至崇信館，九十里至廣寧館，五十里至姚家寨館，五十里至咸寧館，三十里度潢水石橋，旁有饒州，唐於契丹嘗置饒濼州，今渤海人居之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Song Dazhong Xiangfu, Xue Ying's Record says: from Zhongjing due north eighty li to Songshan Station, seventy li to Chongxin Station, ninety li to Guangning Station, fifty li to Yaojiazhai Station, fifty li to Xianning Station, thirty li crossing the Huang River stone bridge—beside it Rao Prefecture, where Tang once placed Rao Marsh Prefecture and Bohai now lived.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ying's Record of Song Dazhong Xiangfu year 9 describes the route north from Zhongjing: eighty li to Songshan Station, seventy to Chongxin, ninety to Guangning, fifty to Yaojiazhai, fifty to Xianning, then thirty li over the Huang River stone bridge by Rao Prefecture—Tang's old Rao Marsh seat, now home to Bohai settlers.

sentences.zh: 五十里保和館，度黑水河，七十里宣化館，五十里長泰館。

translations.literal: Fifty li to Baohe Station, crossing Hei River, seventy li to Xuanhua Station, fifty li to Changtai Station.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty li farther lay Baohe Station; crossing the Hei River, seventy li to Xuanhua Station and fifty to Changtai Station.

sentences.zh: 館西二十里有佛舍，民居，即祖州。

translations.literal: Twenty li west of the station was a Buddhist shrine and dwellings—these were Zu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty li west of the station stood a shrine and houses marking Zu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 又四十里至臨潢府，自過崇信館乃契丹舊境，其南奚地也。

translations.literal: Another forty li to Linhuang Prefecture; after passing Chongxin Station one entered old Khitan territory—south of it was Xi land.
translations.idiomatic: Forty li more reached Linhuang Prefecture; beyond Chongxin Station lay the old Khitan heartland, with Xi territory to the south.

sentences.zh: 入西門，門曰金德，內有臨潢館，子城東門曰順陽。

translations.literal: Entering the west gate, the gate called Jinde; within was Linhuang Hostel; the inner east gate called Shunyang.
translations.idiomatic: The west gate Jinde led to Linhuang Hostel inside; the inner east gate was Shunyang.

sentences.zh: 北行至景福門，又至承天門，內有昭德、宣政二殿，與氈廬皆東向。

translations.literal: Going north to Jingfu Gate, then to Chengtian Gate; within were Zhaode and Xuanzheng halls; with felt tents all faced east.
translations.idiomatic: Northward lay Jingfu Gate, then Chengtian Gate; inside stood Zhaode and Xuanzheng halls, all facing east like the felt tents.

sentences.zh: 臨潢西北二百餘里號涼澱，在饅頭山南，避暑之處。

translations.literal: Northwest of Linhuang more than two hundred li was called Liangdian, south of Mantou Mountain—a place to escape summer heat.
translations.idiomatic: More than two hundred li northwest of Linhuang lay Liangdian south of Mantou Mountain, a summer retreat.

sentences.zh: 多豐草，掘地丈餘即有堅冰。

translations.literal: Grass was abundant; digging a zhang or more down brought hard ice.
translations.idiomatic: Pasture was rich; a zhang below ground one struck hard ice.

translations.literal: Zu Prefecture, Tiancheng Army, upper grade, military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Prefecture—Tiancheng Army, upper grade, with a military commissioner.

translations.literal: Originally the hereditary lands of the Liao Right Eight Divisions.
translations.idiomatic: It had been the hereditary domain of the Liao Right Eight Divisions.

sentences.zh: 太祖秋獵多於此，始置西樓。

translations.literal: Taizu often autumn-hunted here and first set up Xilou.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu hunted here each autumn and first established Xilou.

translations.literal: Later a city was built and called Zu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: A city followed, named Zu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以高祖昭烈皇帝、曾祖莊敬皇帝、祖考簡獻皇帝、皇考宣簡皇帝所生之地，故名。

translations.literal: Because it was the birthplace of the High Ancestor Zhaolie Emperor, the Great-Grandfather Zhuangjing Emperor, the Grandfather Jianxian Emperor, and the Imperial Father Xuanjian Emperor, it took this name.
translations.idiomatic: It commemorated the birthplaces of the High Ancestor Zhaolie, Great-Grandfather Zhuangjing, Grandfather Jianxian, and Imperial Father Xuanjian emperors.

sentences.zh: 城高二丈，無敵棚，幅員九里。

translations.literal: The wall was two zhang high, without fighting galleries; the circuit nine li.
translations.idiomatic: Walls stood two zhang high without fighting galleries; the circuit ran nine li.

sentences.zh: 門，東曰望京，南曰大夏，西曰液山，北曰興國。

translations.literal: Gates: east Wangjing, south Daxia, west Yeshan, north Xingguo.
translations.idiomatic: Gates were Wangjing east, Daxia south, Yeshan west, and Xingguo north.

translations.literal: In the northwest corner was an inner city.
translations.idiomatic: A northwest inner city lay within the walls.

sentences.zh: 殿曰兩明，奉安祖考御容；

translations.literal: Halls called Liangming, enshrining ancestral portraits;
translations.idiomatic: The Liangming Hall enshrined ancestral portraits;

sentences.zh: 曰二儀，以白金鑄太祖像；

translations.literal: called Eryi, casting Taizu's image in white gold;
translations.idiomatic: the Eryi Hall held a white-gold image of Taizu;

sentences.zh: 曰黑龍，曰清秘，各有太祖微時兵仗器物及服御皮毳之類，存之以示後嗣，使勿忘本。

translations.literal: called Heilong and Qingmi, each keeping Taizu's early weapons, utensils, and fur garments to show posterity and not forget origins.
translations.idiomatic: Heilong and Qingmi halls preserved Taizu's early weapons, gear, and furs so posterity would not forget their roots.

sentences.zh: 內南門曰興聖，凡三門，上有樓閣，東西有角樓。

translations.literal: The inner south gate was Xingsheng; three gates in all had tower-pavilions; east and west had corner towers.
translations.idiomatic: The inner south gate Xingsheng headed three gated towers; corner towers stood east and west.

sentences.zh: 東為州廨及諸宮廨舍，綾錦院班院祗侯蕃，漢、渤海三百人，供給內府取索。

translations.literal: East were the prefectural offices and various palace offices; the Brocade Office shift and attendants—Fan, Han, and Bohai three hundred persons—supplied the inner palace on demand.
translations.idiomatic: East lay prefectural offices and palace bureaus; brocade shifts and attendants—three hundred Fan, Han, and Bohai staff—met inner-palace requisitions.

sentences.zh: 東南橫街，四隅有樓對峙，下連市肆。

translations.literal: On the southeast cross street the four corners had facing towers linked to market stalls below.
translations.idiomatic: Along the southeast cross street corner towers faced one another above linked market rows.

translations.literal: East Changba County, west Xianning County.
translations.idiomatic: East stood Changba County; west, Xianning County.

sentences.zh: 有祖山，山有太祖天皇帝廟，禦靴尚存。

translations.literal: There was Zu Mountain with Taizu's Heavenly Emperor Temple; his riding boots still remained.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Mountain held Taizu's Heavenly Emperor Temple, where his riding boots were still kept.

sentences.zh: 又有龍門、黎谷、液山、液泉、白馬、獨石、天梯之山。

translations.literal: There were also Longmen, Ligu, Yeshan, Yequan, Baima, Dushi, and Tianti mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Landmarks included Longmen, Ligu, Yeshan, Yequan, Baima, Dushi, and Tianti peaks.

translations.literal: Waters were the south Sha River and west Yequan.
translations.idiomatic: Waters included the south Sha River and west Yequan.

sentences.zh: 太祖陵鑿山為殿，曰明殿。

translations.literal: Taizu's tomb carved the mountain into a hall called Ming Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu's tomb hollowed the mountain into the Ming Hall.

sentences.zh: 殿南嶺有膳堂，以備時祭。

translations.literal: South of the hall on the ridge was a feast hall for seasonal sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: A feast hall on the southern ridge served seasonal rites.

translations.literal: The gate was called Heilong.
translations.idiomatic: Its gate was named Heilong.

sentences.zh: 東偏有聖蹤殿，立碑述太祖遊獵之事。

translations.literal: To the east was Shengji Hall with a stele describing Taizu's hunting.
translations.idiomatic: East lay Shengji Hall, whose stele recorded Taizu's hunts.

sentences.zh: 殿東有樓，立碑以紀太祖創業之功。

translations.literal: East of the hall was a tower with a stele commemorating Taizu's founding achievement.
translations.idiomatic: East of the hall a tower bore a stele on Taizu's founding deeds.

translations.literal: All were five li west of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: All lay five li west of the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 天顯中太宗建，隸弘義宮。

translations.literal: Built in the Tianxian era by Taizong; subordinate to Hongyi Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong built it in the Tianxian era; it belonged to Hongyi Palace.

translations.literal: It ruled two counties and one walled town: Changba County.
translations.idiomatic: It governed two counties and one walled town—Changba County.

sentences.zh: 本龍州長平縣民，遷於此。

translations.literal: Originally people of Longzhou's Changping County, moved here.
translations.idiomatic: Settlers came from Longzhou's Changping County.

translations.literal: Households 2,000.
translations.idiomatic: 2,000 households.

translations.literal: Xianning County.
translations.idiomatic: County seat: Xianning.

translations.literal: Originally Changning County.
translations.idiomatic: It had been Changning County.

translations.literal: When Liaoyang was taken its people were moved and settled.
translations.idiomatic: After Liaoyang fell its people were resettled here.

translations.literal: Households 1,000.
translations.idiomatic: 1,000 households.

translations.literal: Prince of Yue walled town.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yue Fortified Town.

sentences.zh: 太祖伯父於越王述魯西伐党項、吐渾，俘其民放牧於此，因建城。

translations.literal: Taizu's paternal uncle, campaigning west against Tangut and Tuhun, herded captives here and therefore built a city.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu's paternal uncle, campaigning west against Tangut and Tuhun, pastured captives here and walled a town.

translations.literal: It lay twenty li southeast of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: It stood twenty li southeast of the prefecture.

translations.literal: Households 1,000.
translations.idiomatic: 1,000 households.

translations.literal: Fuyu County.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyu County.

translations.literal: Originally Longquan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: It had been Longquan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太祖遷渤海扶餘縣降戶於此，世宗置縣。

translations.literal: Taizu moved surrendered Bohai Fuyu County households here; Shizong established the county.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu resettled surrendered Bohai households from Fuyu County; Shizong created the county.

translations.literal: Households 1,500.
translations.idiomatic: 1,500 households.

translations.literal: Xianli County.
translations.idiomatic: Xianli County.

sentences.zh: 本顯理府人，太祖伐渤海，俘其王大諲譔，遷民於此，世宗置縣。

translations.literal: Originally people of Xianli Prefecture; Taizu attacked Bohai, captured King Da Yinzhen, and moved the people here; Shizong established the county.
translations.idiomatic: Originally Xianli Prefecture people; when Taizu conquered Bohai and seized King Da Yinzhen he resettled them here; Shizong founded the county.

translations.literal: Households 1,000.
translations.idiomatic: 1,000 households.

translations.literal: Qing Prefecture, Xuanning Army, upper grade, military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Qing Prefecture—Xuanning Army, upper grade, with a military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 本太保山黑河之地，巖谷險峻。

translations.literal: Originally the land of Taibao Mountain and Hei River; valleys and passes were steep and narrow.
translations.idiomatic: Its soil was Taibao Mountain and the Hei River country—rugged valleys and narrow passes.

sentences.zh: 穆宗建城，號黑河州，每歲來幸，射虎障鷹，軍國之事，多委大臣。

translations.literal: Muzong built a city called Hei River Prefecture; each year he came to hunt tigers and hawk eagles, and most military affairs were entrusted to great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong walled Hei River Prefecture, visited yearly to hunt tigers and hawks, and left most military affairs to senior ministers.

translations.literal: Later he was assassinated here.
translations.idiomatic: He was later assassinated on this ground.

sentences.zh: 以地苦寒，統和八年，州廢。

translations.literal: Because the land was bitter cold, in the eighth year of Tonghe the prefecture was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The bitter cold led Tonghe year 8 to abolish the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 聖宗秋畋，愛其奇秀，建號慶州。

translations.literal: Shengzong autumn-hunted, loved its strange beauty, and established the name Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shengzong hunted here in autumn, admired its rugged beauty, and revived it as Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遼國五代祖勃突，貌異常，有武略，力敵百人，眾推為王。

translations.literal: Liao's fifth-generation ancestor Botu had an unusual appearance, martial stratagem, strength to match a hundred men, and the masses pushed him as king.
translations.idiomatic: Liao's fifth-generation ancestor Botu looked unlike others, possessed martial cunning, strength to match a hundred men, and was acclaimed king.

sentences.zh: 生於勃突山，因以名，沒，葬山下。

translations.literal: Born on Botu Mountain, it took the name; when he died he was buried below the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He was born on Botu Mountain, which gave its name; at death he was buried beneath it.

translations.literal: It was two hundred li from the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain lay two hundred li from the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: Qingyun Mountain was originally Heiling.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyun Mountain had formerly been Heiling.

sentences.zh: 聖宗駐蹕，愛羨曰：「吾萬歲後，當葬此」。

translations.literal: Shengzong halted and admired it, saying: "After my ten thousand years I shall be buried here."
translations.idiomatic: Shengzong paused there and said, "When my ten thousand years are fulfilled, bury me here."

translations.literal: Xingzong followed the testament and built Yongqing Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong obeyed the command and built Yongqing Tomb.

translations.literal: There were Wangxian Hall and imperial portrait hall.
translations.idiomatic: It held Wangxian Hall and a hall for imperial portraits.

sentences.zh: 置蕃、漢守陵三千戶，並隸大內都總管司。

translations.literal: Three thousand Fan and Han tomb-guard households were set, all subordinate to the Great Inner Chief Steward Office.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand Fan and Han tomb-guard households were assigned under the Great Inner chief steward.

translations.literal: Twenty li west of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: It lay twenty li west of the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 有黑山、赤山、太保山、老翁嶺、饅頭山、興國湖、轄失濼、黑河。

translations.literal: There were Hei Mountain, Chi Mountain, Taibao Mountain, Laoweng Ridge, Mantou Mountain, Xingguo Lake, Xiaoshi Marsh, and Hei River.
translations.idiomatic: Features included Hei, Chi, and Taibao mountains, Laoweng Ridge, Mantou Mountain, Xingguo Lake, Xiaoshi Marsh, and the Hei River.

sentences.zh: 景福元年復置，更隸興聖宮。

translations.literal: Restored in the first year of Jingfu; later subordinate to Xingsheng Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Restored in Jingfu year 1 and later attached to Xingsheng Palace.

translations.literal: It ruled three counties:
translations.idiomatic: It governed three counties:

translations.literal: Xuande County.
translations.idiomatic: Xuande County.

translations.literal: Originally Hei Mountain and Hei River land.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the Hei Mountain and Hei River region.

sentences.zh: 景福元年，括落帳人戶，從便居之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingfu, scattered-account households were gathered and settled as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Jingfu year 1 gathered scattered-account households for settlement where convenient.

translations.literal: Households 6,000.
translations.idiomatic: 6,000 households.

translations.literal: Xiao'an County.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao'an County.

translations.literal: Fuyi County.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyi County.

sentences.zh: 本義州，太宗遷渤海義州民於此。

translations.literal: Originally Yi Prefecture; Taizong moved Bohai Yi Prefecture people here.
translations.idiomatic: Originally Yi Prefecture; Taizong resettled Bohai people from Yi Prefecture here.
